defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a made-up run with a fixed seed, so it comes out the same every time.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: First ask whether the case has a contract, or only a split of the work.
An appropriate contract has testable handoffs and a declared route for failure.
Phase gates and delegation buckets show whether the steps are appropriate.
Find every check, who does it, and the artifact that proves it happened.
Judge the evaluator by comparing the override rate with the audited error rate.
Then say it exactly, three ticks and one of four codes, not a vague review.
bookends.command: Give me short delegation cases, one at a time. For each, I answer four questions. Is there a contract, and is it appropriate? Are the steps appropriate? Where are the checks, and who does them? Who evaluates, and is that appropriate? I must name the exact terms, handoff condition, testable, failure routing, delegation buckets, verification cost, unsupervised pipeline, sign-off authority and overtrust. Hold back your answer until I reply, then correct me in two sentences.
checks: Check: every case asks about contract, steps, checks and who evaluates.
Check: each answer is held back until you name the exact terms.
